Last week, Coyote vs. ACME proved Warner Bros. wrong by earning more than the company's $30 million tax write-off. Now, the latest Looney Tunes film has shown demand, hitting another milestone just 48 hours before it enters other markets, thus proving a consensus among fans online that this media conglomerate has no idea what fans want. Could this be a sign the company should pay more attention to its target audience?

Coyote vs. ACME is a live-action/animated hybrid legal comedy where Wile E. Coyote sues ACME for all their malfunctioning products, but his lawyer doesn't know the lawsuit was just a ploy to catch the Road Runner. As the case draws public attention, it is later revealed that a conspiracy was at work behind the scenes, showing that ACME has done more harm than just "cartoon injury." Warner Bros. initially pulled the feature from its release, along with other highly anticipated projects like Batgirl, but after backlash and a campaign to bring it to the big screen, Warner Bros. let the filmmakers find a new distributor, saving the film.

Last week, Coyote vs. ACME earned more than Warner Bros.' tax write-off. This week, it has officially surpassed its production budget. Cartoon Brew reported that Coyote vs. ACME has grossed more than $82.8 million worldwide after three weekends, exceeding its reported $70–72 million production budget. The film is also set to expand to more theaters this week, so its box office total could keep growing as more audiences get the chance to see it.

Is 'Coyote Vs. ACME' Worth Watching?

Since its release, Coyote vs. ACME has earned a 96% Certified Fresh critics' score and a 95% Verified Hot audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, plus a 3.9-star rating on Letterboxd. Critics praised Coyote vs. ACME as entertaining and noted room for "childish whimsy." They also praised the film for turning Coyote into a role model and for its relevance to current events. ScreenRant claimed that the filmmakers "clearly understood the appeal of Looney Tunes" and praised Will Forte and John Cena's performances as Kevin Averey and Buddy Craine, respectively. CBR also praised the cast's performances, especially Cena.

Meanwhile, audiences enjoyed it for its nostalgia and the new elements it added to the Coyote and Road Runner skits, and claimed it's one of the "best Looney Tunes films out there." Collider's Taylor Gates gave Coyote vs. ACME an 8/10 in her review, praising the film's comedy, themes, and emotional storytelling, but criticized some of the gags.
